To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

both amphetamine sensitization (a rodent model of addiction) and gestational methylazoymethanol acetate (a rodent prenatal model of schizophrenia) display enhanced ventromedial striatum dopamine system activity.

both amphetamine sensitization in rats and gestational methylazymethanol acetates (MAM)-induced schizophrenia in rats are associated with increased activity of dopamine neurons in the medial part of the ventral tegmentum (VTA) that project to the ventral striatum (VST) but only MAM is associated with an increase in dopamine neurons activity in the ventrolateral part of the VTA that project to the dorsal striatum (DST).

(1) amphetamine sensitization increases the activity of the ventromedial dopamine neurons that project to ventromedial striatum, and (2) MAM treatment increases the activity of both the ventromedially and the ventrolaterally projecting dopamine neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the dopamine system in the pathogenesis of schizophrenia and addiction.
understanding the neurobiological mechanisms underlying the pathophysiology of schizophrenia and substance abuse.
the neurobiology of schizophrenia and substance use disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the VTA-ventral striatal dopamine system is not a homogeneous entity and that its function can be differentially altered by a number of different disease states, including amphetamine sensitization, schizophrenia and Parkinson's disease.
the VTA dopamine neurons are not a homogeneous population of neurons.
the VTA-VM striatal dopamine system is hyperactive, while the VTA- VL striatal dopamine system may be either hyperactive or hypoactive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

schizophrenia and amphetamine sensitization are associated with a similar pattern of increased dopamine neuron activity in the ventromedial VTA, but that only schizophrenia is associated with increased ventrolateral VTA neuron activity.

schizophrenia and amphetamine sensitization share a common mechanism of increased dopamine neuron population activity within the medial VTA, but only MAM-treated animals display a hyperdopamine state in the ventrolateral VTA.
the medial VTA-VM striatal pathway is hyperactivated in both amphetamine sensitized animals and MAM treated animals, while the VTA-VL striatal pathway is only hyperactivated in MAM treated animals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the VTA dopamine neurons are not a homogeneous population.

, although there is an increase in dopamine activity in both schizophrenia and amphetamine sensitization, there is a divergence in the populations of neurons affected, which probably underlies the differences in disease symptoms.

, although there is a hyperdopamine state in both amphetamine sensitization (a model of drug addiction) and schizophrenia, the hyperdopamine system is not the same in both models, and that the differences in the hyperdopaminergics state may underlie the differences in the behavioural phenotypes observed in these two models.
